extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, inventors, and patent practitioners interacting with USPTO micro entity rules and public facility procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for claiming, maintaining, correcting, and forfeiting micro entity status (including the institution-of-higher-education basis), plus related USPTO facility and filing rules referenced on these pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity status — institution of higher education basis (37 CFR 1.29(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for micro entity status under the “institution of higher education” basis set forth in 37 CFR 1.29(d) must satisfy two requirements: (1) certify that the applicant qualifies as a small entity as defined in 37 CFR 1.27; and (2) certify that either (i) the applicant’s employer, from which the applicant obtains the majority of the applicant’s income, is an institution of higher education as defined in section 101(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001(a)); or (ii) the applicant has assigned, granted, conveyed, or is under an obligation by contract or law, to assign, grant, or convey, a license or other ownership interest in the particular application to such an institution of higher education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.29(d)(1) requires certification of small entity status in addition to the institution-of-higher-education certification. The PTO implements 35 U.S.C. 123(d) via 37 CFR 1.29(d). Use PTO/SB/15B for the required certifications. See MPEP §509.02 for small entity rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity requirement for micro entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet the small entity requirement, every party holding rights in the application must qualify as a small entity under 37 CFR 1.27. If any rights in the application are assigned, granted, conveyed, or licensed to a party that does not qualify as a small entity under 37 CFR 1.27, the applicant cannot qualify for any patent fee discount. An obligation to assign, grant, convey, or license rights in the application to a party that does not qualify for small entity status also disqualifies the applicant from receiving any patent fee discount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There can be no party holding rights or obligated rights in the application that does not qualify as a small entity. See MPEP §509.02 for details on small entity status and the §1.27 rules and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personhood of certifier for employer-based certification (37 CFR 1.29(d)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Because only a person can have an 'employer,' the applicant certifying under 37 CFR 1.29(d)(2)(i) must be a person or persons, which in most cases means the inventor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For joint inventor applicants, each joint inventor should sign a separate copy of the relevant micro entity certification form unless one joint inventor is appointed to prosecute on behalf of all (then only that inventor need sign). See PTO form PTO/AIA/81 for power of attorney procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sham or de minimis transfers to obtain micro entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: An attempt to obtain micro entity status by merely seeking to transfer a de minimis interest to an institution of higher education could be considered a sham transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will monitor percentages of applicants claiming micro entity status under 35 U.S.C. 123(d) to ensure such transactions are not used to obtain status improperly. Anti-pattern: arranging token transfers or sham assignments solely to claim micro entity benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'institution of higher education' (HEA §101(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'institution of higher education' means an educational institution in any State that: (1) admits as regular students only persons with secondary education certificates or recognized equivalent; (2) is legally authorized within such State to provide a program of education beyond secondary education; (3) provides an educational program awarding a bachelor’s degree or at least a 2-year program acceptable for full credit toward such a degree, or awards a degree acceptable for admission to graduate or professional programs; (4) is a public or other nonprofit institution; and (5) is accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency or, if pre-accredited, has satisfactory assurance of meeting accreditation standards within a reasonable time. 'State' includes the 50 states and listed territories and Freely Associated States per 20 U.S.C. 1003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public or nonprofit institutions located in the U.S. or territories offering qualifying undergraduate programs meet the definition. Non-profit status and accreditation are key elements; institutions such as non-profit research foundations, tech transfer organizations, or Federal Government research laboratories do not qualify as 'institutions of higher education' for micro entity purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities and colleges that do not qualify as institutions of higher education
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit universities and colleges do not qualify as an 'institution of higher education' for purposes of establishing micro entity status. Foreign universities do not qualify. Institutions that only grant graduate degrees do not qualify because HEA §101(a) requires undergraduate programs awarding bachelor’s or at least 2‑year programs acceptable toward a bachelor’s degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A foreign university offering on-line programs in the United States does not qualify the foreign university as an 'institution of higher education' for micro entity purposes because the institution must be located 'in any State' as meant in 1965. Online classes alone do not establish qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: University cannot be the micro entity applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Although 37 CFR 1.29(d) is referred to as the 'institution of higher education' basis, it is not the institution that can qualify for micro entity status; rather inventors who are employees of an institution of higher education (37 CFR 1.29(d)(2)(i)) or inventors/applicants who have conveyed ownership rights to an institution (37 CFR 1.29(d)(2)(ii)) can qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution (university) cannot make the certifications required under 37 CFR 1.29(d)(2)(i) and (d)(2)(ii). The certifications must be made by persons (inventors/applicants) as required by the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification form (PTO/SB/15B) and signature blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO/SB/15B contains the certifications under 37 CFR 1.29(d) required to establish micro entity status on the institution of higher education basis. There are two signature blocks reflecting the small entity requirement and the two alternative requirements under 37 CFR 1.29(d)(2): one for certifying under 1.29(d)(2)(i) (employer majority income from an institution) and one for certifying under 1.29(d)(2)(ii) (assignment/grant/conveyance to such institution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate signature block corresponding to the alternative you are certifying. Ensure signatures follow the signatory rules in 37 CFR 1.33(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized signatories for micro entity certification (37 CFR 1.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification of micro entity status, on either the gross income basis or the institution of higher education basis, can be signed only by an authorized party as set forth in 37 CFR 1.33(b): (1) a patent practitioner of record; (2) a patent practitioner not of record who acts in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34; or (3) the applicant (37 CFR 1.42). Unless otherwise specified, all papers submitted on behalf of a juristic entity must be signed by a patent practitioner. If any applicant is an assignee or other party under 37 CFR 1.46 and that assignee is a corporation or organization, a registered practitioner must sign the certification; an officer of the assignee corporation is not authorized to sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For joint inventor applicants, follow the joint-inventor signing guidance. Registered practitioners must sign for juristic entities. Unauthorized signers (e.g., corporate officers for assignees) are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued obligation to determine micro entity qualification (37 CFR 1.29(g)-(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification of entitlement to micro entity status need only be filed once in an application or patent and remains in effect until changed pursuant to paragraph (i). However, a fee may be paid in the micro entity amount only if status as a micro entity is appropriate on the date the fee is being paid. Prior to submitting a certification, a determination of entitlement should be made that each applicant qualifies for micro entity status under 1.29(a) or (d) and that any other party holding rights qualifies for small entity status under §1.27. For gross income basis claims, a new determination must be made each year because gross income may change; determine that no inventor's gross income exceeds the maximum qualifying gross income and that no assignments to entities exceeding the maximum qualifying gross income exist. For 35 U.S.C. 123(d) claims, determine that applicants still obtain the majority of income from an institution of higher education as defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Micro entity status is evaluated at each fee payment date. Check the USPTO website for 'maximum qualifying gross income' annually. The Office generally will not question certifications made in accordance with requirements, but applicants must re-evaluate eligibility before each micro-fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of loss of entitlement to micro entity status (37 CFR 1.29(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of a loss of entitlement to micro entity status must be filed in the application or patent prior to paying, or at the time of paying, any fee after the date on which micro entity status is no longer appropriate. The notification must be signed by an authorized party identified in §1.33(b). Payment of a fee in other than the micro entity amount is not sufficient notification. A notification that micro entity status is no longer appropriate will not be treated as a notification that small entity status is also no longer appropriate unless it also contains such notification. Once a notification is filed, a new certification is required to again obtain micro entity status. Form SB/460 may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant can make a simple statement that they are no longer eligible without identifying specific reasons. Filing the notification converts subsequent fee payments to the appropriate (non-micro) fee amounts unless and until a new micro certification is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting errors in micro entity status and deficiency payments (37 CFR 1.29(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: If micro entity status and micro-fee payments were established in good faith but later discovered to be in error or if the Office was not notified of a loss of entitlement, the error will be excused upon compliance with submission and itemization requirements of 1.29(k)(1) and payment of the deficiency under 1.29(k)(2). The paper must be limited to the deficiency payment for a single application or patent and must itemize: (i) each particular type of fee erroneously paid as a micro entity and the current small/non-small fee amount; (ii) the micro entity fee actually paid and the date; (iii) the deficiency owed amount for each fee; and (iv) the total deficiency payment owed. The deficiency owed for each fee is the difference between the current fee amount for a small or non-small entity and the previous erroneous micro entity fee payment. Failure to comply may result in the Office processing the deficiency and charging a processing fee under 1.17(i), or requiring compliance within a one-month non-extendable period under 1.136(a). Any deficiency payment submitted under 1.29(k) will be treated as a notification of loss of entitlement under 1.29(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate submissions and itemizations are required where more than one application or patent is involved. This provision parallels the small-entity correction procedures under 37 CFR 1.28(c). Keep documentation precise to avoid additional processing fees or return of payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO business hours and filing during unscheduled closings (37 CFR 1.6, 1.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: US PTO working hours are 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays in the District of Columbia. When the entire USPTO is officially closed for the day (e.g., adverse weather), that day is treated as a 'Federal holiday within the District of Columbia' under 35 U.S.C. 21 and actions/fees due on that day may be taken or paid on the next succeeding business day the Office is open. 37 CFR 1.6(a)(2) and 1.10 provide that correspondence deposited as Priority Mail Express® with the USPS will be considered filed on the date of deposit even if that date is a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday. Under 37 CFR 1.10(g), if Priority Mail Express® correspondence is returned due to interruption or emergency in service, a petition may be filed promptly to have the correspondence considered filed on a particular date, provided the petition is filed promptly and the Priority Mail Express® mailing label number was placed on the papers prior to mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing during potential postal interruptions, use Priority Mail Express® and retain label numbers. Contact USPTO information lines for closure announcements. The deposit-date rule can preserve filing dates; follow petition requirements promptly if mail is returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct and access rules for public information and Technology Center (TC) facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to USPTO public information facilities requires a valid Public User or Visitor’s badge and an On-line Service Card for online systems. User badges are nontransferable and valid until reissue or revocation. Persons violating regulations governing public conduct on Office premises may be denied use of facilities and may be prosecuted; names of registered persons violating rules may be forwarded to Enrollment and Discipline under 37 CFR Part 11. Authorized members using TC facilities must follow additional rules: (1) no USPTO records or documents may be removed except by written authorization from an authorized TC official; (2) use of equipment (dictation, reproducing, photographic, etc.) is prohibited without prior permission from an authorized official in the TC; (3) packages, briefcases, or personal effects brought into TC facilities are subject to search and must be removed when leaving; (4) verbal requests for compliance with regulations by authorized officials must be promptly complied with; (5) Supervisory Patent Examiners and TC Directors may demand surrender of a User or Visitor badge on-the-spot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations should be reported to supervisors who prepare memos and forward them up the chain; immediate courteous requests for compliance are appropriate. Refusal to comply may result in denial of facility use, criminal prosecution, or disciplinary action for registered practitioners. Supervisors should document incidents and notify the TC Director and appropriate chain of command.
